items.title: Cyber Security Authority: Ghana led Operation Blackout, not FBI
items.description: The Cyber Security Authority (CSA) has rejected claims by the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) that the cybercrime operation carried out in Ghana this week was conceived, commanded or executed by the bureau. In a press release issued on Thursday, October 8, 2026, the authority said the operation, also referred to as Operation Cyber Hunt, was led and coordinated by Ghana’s Cyber Security Authority. It said the operation was conducted with support from Ghana’s National Security Council, the Criminal Investigations Department of the Ghana Police Service, the National Crime Agency of the United Kingdom, the FBI, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission of Nigeria, the Joint Case Team on Cybercrime, the Ghana Immigration Service and the Office of the Attorney-General. The authority said Ghanaian authorities planned, coordinated and executed the operation within Ghana’s legal and institutional frameworks. It said the operation could not be said to have been conceived as part of an FBI-led global programme, nor was it conducted under a foreign operational command. It stated that Ghana is a sovereign republic governed by its Constitution and laws, and that foreign law enforcement agencies have no independent authority to exercise police powers or conduct arrests within Ghana. It said their participation must take place through lawful cooperation, with the authorisation and involvement of relevant Ghanaian authorities. The authority acknowledged the intelligence contributions of the FBI and the National Crime Agency, saying the partnerships remain important to effective investigations and operations. It, however, said the contribution of international partners must be described accurately. It called on the FBI to clarify its public account of the Ghana-led operation and to acknowledge the contributions of the Ghanaian institutions and other international partners responsible for its execution. The authority said it remained available for constructive engagement to ensure the public record reflects the respective roles of all participating agencies. The authority said the operation uncovered suspected cybercrime centres in parts of the Greater Accra Region. Eight suspects were arrested, and one hundred and twenty others suspected to have been trafficked and exploited for online fraud activities were rescued. It said the operation followed intelligence received on August 26, 2026, indicating that several apartments at Ubuntu Haven Estate in Kpone Katamanso, Franko Estate in Ga North and other locations in Ga West were being used as bases for organised cybercrime, including romance scams. Items seized included 136 mobile phones, 130 laptops, internet connection devices, four motor vehicles, one of which was stolen from Canada, and other digital equipment. The search team also recovered jewellery and ten Nigerian passports. The authority said it was working to repatriate the rescued victims, identified largely as Nigerians, while investigations into the suspects and the seized devices are ongoing. It reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to dismantling cybercriminal networks and protecting the public from online fraud. It said it would continue to strengthen intelligence-led investigations, inter-agency coordination, digital forensic capabilities and international cooperation.

items.title: L'OMM alerte sur un épisode El Niño d'une intensité historique d'ici la fin de l'année
items.description: Le réchauffement du Pacifique tropical atteint des proportions inédites qui alarment la communauté scientifique internationale. Dans une mise en garde, l’Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM) a averti que l’épisode El Niño actuellement en cours pourrait enregistrer des pics de température jamais observés depuis le début des relevés en 1950, accentuant drastiquement les risques de sécheresses extrêmes, d'inondations dévastatrices et de vagues de chaleur à l'échelle planétaire. Selon les projections convergentes de 13 centres météorologiques internationaux appuyées par l'agence onusienne, la probabilité que le phénomène persiste jusqu’en février 2027 avoisine les 100 %. Les indicateurs statistiques témoignent d'une accélération fulgurante : alors que l'anomalie thermique de la surface des mers dans le Pacifique équatorial s'établissait à +1,6 °C en juin et +2,5 °C en août, l'OMM anticipe un écart moyen de +3,7 °C sur la période d'octobre à décembre. Un chiffre qui pulvérise le précédent record de +2,6 °C mesuré lors de la crise climatique de 2015-2016. Cette surchauffe exceptionnelle survient dans un contexte mondial déjà fragilisé par le réchauffement anthropique. Comme l'a souligné Celeste Saulo, secrétaire générale de l'OMM lors du Forum mondial sur la chaleur à Bangkok, El Niño agit comme un accélérateur en libérant dans l'atmosphère d'immenses quantités de chaleur emmagasinées par des océans ayant déjà atteint des températures maximales absolues en août 2026. Ce dérèglement à grande échelle dessine une carte des risques mondiaux fortement contrastée d'ici la fin de l'année. Des précipitations excédentaires et des risques de crues menacent la Corne de l’Afrique, le nord de la péninsule Arabique, l'Asie centrale et certaines zones des Amériques, à l'instar de la Californie qui renforce ses dispositifs d'urgence. À l'inverse, un déficit pluviométrique sévère menace le sous-continent indien, le sud de l'Amérique centrale et les Caraïbes, faisant peser de lourdes incertitudes sur les récoltes agricoles et la sécurité alimentaire mondiale. Face à cette menace imminente, l'OMM appelle les gouvernements à opérationnaliser sans délai leurs plans de prévention et d'action humanitaire anticipée. D’un coût global de 254,79 milliards francs CFA, cette initiative du gouvernement vise à r éaliser 750 forages afin de renforcer l’accès des producteurs à l’eau et de soutenir la production agricole en saison sèche. Le démarrage des premières forations est prévu pour le 25 octobre 2026 et l’opération continuera jusqu’en novembre prochain. Des cadres du ministère burkinabè de l’Agriculture, de l'Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, étaient face à la presse dans la soirée du jeudi 8 octobre 2026 au siège du Département ministériel sis à Ouaga 2000. Au cours des échanges, les conférenciers ont annoncé la décision du gouvernement via leur ministère de réaliser un plan d’urgence pour contrer la saison pluvieuse qui est en demi-teinte dans plusieurs parties du pays. Après l’Offensive agropastorale et halieutique (OAPH), le ministère du commandant Ismaël Sombié veut se dresser contre la saison sèche qui n’est pas rassurante à certains endroits dans le pays. Ainsi, selon le directeur général de Faso Agropole (SOFA), Damien Oula Ouattara, le Département lance le cadre du plan d’urgence de la campagne sèche 2026-2027 en vue de réaliser «750 forages» à prix subventionnés pour renforcer l’accès des producteurs à l’eau et de soutenir la production agricole en saison sèche. En plus des forages, l’opération vise également la réalisation de l’équipement de 1 000 bas-fonds avec des forages et la mise en exploitation des parcelles situées autour des points d’eau. Par cette initiative, les autorités veulent passer des 30 000 hectares de périmètres irrigués opérationnels à une superficie de 80 000 hectares au 31 octobre 2027, soit une augmentation de 50 000 hectares à aménager pour accroître les capacités nationales de production agricole qui va nécessiter le recrutement de 8 000 volontaires agricoles pour les travaux champêtres. Une vue des conférenciers. Le DG de Faso Agropole (SOFA), Damien Oula Ouattara (2e à gauche) Dans cette opération, l’Etat prendra en charge la foration qui sera entièrement gratuite pour le producteur. Pour chaque bénéficiaire, l’État prend en charge précisément «la foration pour un seul essai; le développement du forage; le tubage PVC et sa pose; l’essai de pompage; l’analyse de l’eau et l’accompagnement technique pour l’installation de la pompe», a déclaré M. Ouattara qui a ajouté qu’un forage réalisé devra présenter un débit minimum de 5 m³/h. Mais, les conférenciers se veulent clairs: en cas de forage négatif, aucune reprise ne sera prévue. A ce niveau, le bénéficiaire doit, pour sa part, prendre en charge «la prospection géophysique préalable; la pompe immergée; le champ solaire et les accessoires d’exhaure», a poursuivi le Directeur général de la SOFA, soulignant que l’opération est ouverte à tous les Burkinabè, notamment les personnes physiques et les organisations de producteurs régulièrement constituées. Autres précisions de taille, le conférencier principal a indiqué que pour être éligible, le candidat doit notamment «exploiter au moins 2 hectares; disposer d’un droit foncier sur le site; produire une spéculation relevant des filières de l’Offensive 2026-2028; réaliser la prospection géophysique; disposer des équipements d’exhaure avant la foration et s’engager à entretenir et à exploiter l’ouvrage». Par Bernard BOUGOUM L’article Burkina: un plan d’urgence pour la campagne sèche 2026-2027 de près de 255 milliards FCFA annoncé est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Le Premier ministre néerlandais dans la tourmente après avoir nié au Parlement l’utilisation de l’IA sur ses comptes officiels
items.description: Le Premier ministre neerlandais Rob Jetten a fourni au Parlement des informations inexactes sur son usage de l'intelligence artificielle, affirme le quotidien de Volkskrant . Une nouvelle enquete porte sur cinq publications diffusees sur ses comptes officiels. Le 29 septembre, Jetten avait assure a la Chambre des representants qu'« aucune IA n'avait ete utilisee » sur ces comptes. En septembre, le journal avait deja revele que le dirigeant et son parti, D66, avaient utilise cette technologie pour produire des centaines de messages sur les reseaux sociaux. Les comptes rendus de cette premiere enquete evoquaient notamment des publications sur le conflit en Ukraine et le crash du vol MH17 en 2014. Mais, au cœur de la polemique, figure surtout la distinction etablie par le gouvernement entre les comptes personnels de Jetten et ses comptes officiels. Cinq messages au cœur de l'enquete Jetten avait assure a RTL que les textes prepares avec l'IA etaient toujours verifies. Le service d'information du gouvernement (RVD) affirmait que cet usage se limitait aux comptes personnels du dirigeant, geres avec D66, et ne concernait pas ses comptes officiels. Or, selon de Volkskrant , le detecteur Pangram a identifie comme generes par l'IA cinq messages publies sur ces comptes au cours des six derniers mois. Deux experts consultes jugent tres improbable que les cinq resultats soient errones. Ils relevent egalement des tournures et des structures repetitives. Sur 2 000 publications redigees par des humains, le journal a releve un taux de faux positifs de 0,1 %. Le RVD ne nie pas le recours a l'IA, mais conteste que ces textes aient ete entierement produits par cette technologie. Il precise qu'ils s'appuient sur des dossiers politiques, des notes de reunion et des textes anterieurs. Les regles du gouvernement en question Les regles officielles sont egalement en cause. Selon de Volkskrant , les recommandations de 2025 interdisent de reprendre tels quels des textes generes par l'IA et prevoient de signaler les contenus ainsi produits lorsqu'ils sont destines aux citoyens. Aucun des messages examines ne portait cette mention. Le RVD invoque une nouvelle directive dispensant de signalement apres controle humain. Or, selon les metadonnees relevees par le journal, la page presentant cette directive a ete creee le 17 septembre, apres la premiere enquete. Les experts contestent egalement la distinction entre comptes « prives » et « officiels », les publications etant liees aux fonctions de Jetten. Le constitutionnaliste Wim Voermans juge « politiquement inexplicable » une negation categorique si l'usage de l'IA est etabli. Pour le juriste Paul Bovend'eert, un Premier ministre reste responsable, quoi qu'il en soit, de sa communication.

items.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Re0.66 per litre, raises high-speed diesel rate by Re0.52 per litre
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · " style="width: 100%; min-height: 50px; max-height: 30000px; border: none; overflow: hidden; display: block;" scrolling="no"> The government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Re0.66 per litre, but increased that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.52 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs398.30 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.24 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 10 (Saturday) to Oct 12 (Monday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Véhicules importés dépassant la condition d’âge : vers le dédouanement sous conditions
items.description: Le PLF 2027, qui a été adopté dimanche dernier en Conseil des ministres, propose une importante disposition visant à régulariser les véhicules dépassant la condition d'âge à l’importation. La régularisation se fera sous certaines conditions. Ces véhicules, lit-on dans le texte proposé par le gouvernement , sont admis au dédouanement pour la mise à la consommation, sous réserve que le dépassement n’excède pas six mois et que la condition d’âge soit respectée à la date de leur expédition directe à destination du territoire douanier national (article 168). Il est aussi exigé le paiement d’une majoration de 3% des droits et taxes “pour chaque mois ou fraction de mois de dépassement constaté”. Dédouanement des véhicules importés qui ont dépassé la condition d’âge : une taxe de 3% Les véhicules dépassant la condition d’âge requise par la législation et qui ont été introduits dans le territoire algérien avant la publication de la loi de finances pour 2027, seront également admis au dédouanement si la condition d’âge est respectée à la date d’expédition du véhicule. Là aussi, le dédouanement se fait avec application d’une majoration de 3% des droits et taxes exigibles. Le gouvernement indique qu’il a été constaté l’existence d’un nombre considérable de véhicules neufs et d’occasion qui, bien que respectant la condition d'âge à la date de leur expédition directe vers le territoire douanier national, se retrouvent en dépassement de cette condition au moment de souscription de la déclaration en douane, en raison “de délais d'acheminement, de problèmes de logistique internationale, de transit ou de formalités portuaires à l’étranger et des retards résultant de circonstances indépendantes de la volonté de l'importateur”. La mesure vise notamment à résorber le stock de véhicules dans les zones sous douane et désengorger les espaces portuaires. items.title: Sahibzada Farhan hits dazzling 89 as Pakistan down Sri Lanka in first T20I
items.description: Sahibzada Farhan marked his first match as Pakistan’s full-time Twenty20 International captain with a commanding 89 as the hosts chased down Sri Lanka’s 182-8 to secure a four-wicket victory with seven balls to spare in the opening match of the three-game series at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Friday. Farhan struck 10 fours and four sixes in his 53-ball knock, while Maaz Sadaqat smashed a maiden T20I half-century to put Pakistan firmly on course for victory. Their 92-run second-wicket partnership proved decisive as Pakistan reached 187-6 in 18.5 overs. The hosts made a flying start to the 183-run chase, with Farhan and Fakhar Zaman adding 54 for the opening wicket. Fakhar struck four boundaries in his 13-ball 21 before falling to Eshan Malinga in the final over of the powerplay, by which time Pakistan had raced to 70-1. Maaz immediately maintained the momentum, taking advantage of loose deliveries to punish the Sri Lankan bowlers. He swept Maheesh Theekshana past fine leg for four before Farhan launched the spinner for six as Pakistan crossed the 100-run mark in the 10th over. The left-hander continued to attack, smashing Dunith Wellalage over long-on for six before Farhan brought up his half-century off 33 balls. Maaz reached his maiden T20I fifty off just 21 deliveries in the 13th over, striking four fours and three sixes in an innings that gave Pakistan control of the chase. Farhan then took Theekshana apart in the 14th over, sweeping him over long-on for six before adding two more boundaries. The spinner, however, ended Maaz’s 29-ball knock of 50 by trapping him leg-before, leaving Pakistan at 146-2. Sri Lanka briefly threatened to turn the contest around as Hasan Nawaz was caught behind off Dushmantha Chameera for one and Theekshana bowled Saim Ayub for eight in successive overs. Pakistan slipped to 156-4, but Farhan remained the key to the chase. After two quieter overs, the captain attacked Nuwan Thushara in the 18th, striking a boundary through square leg before launching a low full toss over extra cover for six. His innings ended at 89 when he was caught by Sahan Arachchige in the deep off the next delivery, with Pakistan needing just four runs for victory. Shadab Khan fell for a duck, caught off Malinga, but Khawaja Nafay ensured there was no late drama. He finished unbeaten on 12 off seven balls, including a six over long-on, as Pakistan reached their target in 18.5 overs. Mohammad Imran remained not out on nought. Earlier, Sri Lanka had posted 182-8 after winning the toss and electing to bat, with Lahiru Udara anchoring the innings through a superb 91 off 55 balls. The batter struck 11 fours and a six, lifting Sri Lanka from 83-4 after Pakistan’s bowlers had made early inroads. Naseem Shah removed captain Kusal Mendis for one in the opening over, while debutant Mohammad Imran dismissed Kamil Mishara for six. Udara then joined Kamindu Mendis in a counterattack that brought 60 runs for the third wicket. Kamindu made 23 off 18 balls, hitting four boundaries, before falling to Saim, caught by Fakhar at long-off. Two balls later, Sahan Arachchige departed for one after Shadab took a fine catch at point off Imran. Undeterred, Udara brought up his maiden T20I half-century off 32 balls and continued to score freely. Dasun Shanaka contributed 18 off 15 balls, including two sixes, before Fakhar caught him off Shadab with Sri Lanka at 140-5. Udara survived a missed chance on 77 when spinner Abrar Ahmed misjudged a high catch, but his innings ended nine runs short of a century when Naseem had him caught by Hasan at long-on in the final ball of the 19th over. Naseem finished with 3-36 from four overs, while Imran claimed 2-21. Razaullah took his maiden T20I wicket in the final over, dismissing Theekshana for one, before Dushmantha Chameera struck a boundary off a free hit to help Sri Lanka finish on 182-8. Despite Udara’s effort, Pakistan’s aggressive top-order batting proved decisive. Farhan’s captain’s knock and Maaz’s rapid half-century gave the hosts a winning start to the series, while Sri Lanka were left to rue their inability to stem the scoring during the middle overs.

items.title: ‘I may share this prize with Trump’ — Nobel winner Pillay
items.description: South African champion of international law Navi Pillay, who was awarded this year’s Nobel peace prize, joked that she might “share the prize” with US President Donald Trump if people kept applauding her. “If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump,” Pillay said in a video posted to X by the Secretary General of Amnesty International, which showed Pillay being applauded in Nuremberg after the announcement of the award. She said that her first reaction to hearing the news was that it must be a joke. “Being a lawyer and a judge, I still want to verify this,” the 85-year-old said, wanting to make sure it was true. Pillay mentioned her work heading the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry (COI), which does not speak on behalf of the world body, and which last year found that genocide was occurring in Gaza. “The last thing I did is the delivery of the report on Gaza, naming what’s happening there as genocide,” she said. “One of the main reactions to that report is paying tribute to me for my courage. And you can imagine how surprised I was, why would you need courage to speak the truth?” she added. The prize comes with a gold medal, a diploma and a prize sum of $1.2 million. The award will be presented at a formal ceremony in Oslo on December 10, the anniversary of the 1896 death of the prizes’ creator, Swedish inventor and philanthropist Alfred Nobel. The post ‘I may share this prize with Trump’ — Nobel winner Pillay appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Centre done mulling emergency, option to be availed if KP does not cooperate on counter-terrorism: minister
items.description: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said on Friday that the Centre had finished deliberating on the imposition of an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, warning that a lack of provincial government cooperation on counter-terrorism would lead it to enforce an emergency and then eradicate terrorism. The minister made these remarks on Geo New s programme ‘ Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath ’, during which he also refused to confirm reports that a high-level meeting was expected on Saturday to decide on the imposition of an emergency in KP. The Centre has warned the PTI-led KP government in recent days of sending it packing through an emergency or governor’s rule as the party goes ahead with a protest march to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. items.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The African Democratic Congress (ADC) on Friday launched its 2027 presidential campaign with a pledge to reverse the economic hardship Nigerians face, declaring that President Bola Tinubu must be voted out and replaced with former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. The party, which unveiled its Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja, said soaring living costs, insecurity, unemployment and rising public debt had deepened Nigerians’ hardship, insisting that its Atiku Abubakar–Rotimi Amaechi ticket offered a credible alternative. National Chairman, Senator David Mark, Campaign Council Chairman, Kashim Ibrahim-Imam, and Director-General, Senator Austin Akobundu, spoke at the inauguration, charging party members to mobilise nationwide around the promise of affordable living and better governance. Akobundu said the campaign would focus on the daily struggles of families, workers, farmers and business owners, arguing that government policies had made basic necessities increasingly difficult to afford. “Tinubu made life expensive. I will make life affordable again,” Akobundu quoted Atiku as saying. He said Atiku would prioritise local refining through a targeted, budgeted production subsidy for fuel refined in Nigeria, alongside reforms in electricity, education, healthcare and agriculture. The proposed measures, he said, would ease production costs, improve access to essential services and create opportunities for young people and women. Akobundu also pledged to review the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, pursue student debt forgiveness, improve security on farmlands and implement the Supreme Court judgment on local government autonomy. On the political climate, he accused the administration of subjecting ADC members to intimidation and harassment through state agencies, vowing that the party would resist such actions while campaigning within the law. “The ADC will resist every form of intimidation and harassment!” he declared. He also condemned what he described as the continued incarceration of the council’s Deputy Chairman, former Kaduna State governor Nasir El-Rufai, calling it an affront to the rule of law. Ibrahim-Imam delivered the sharpest political attack, declaring that the campaign was a mission to rescue Nigerians from economic hardship and insecurity. “The palace feasts while the people fast!” he said, accusing the Tinubu administration of excessive spending while millions of Nigerians struggled to meet basic needs. Citing figures presented in his address, Ibrahim-Imam said Nigeria’s public debt had risen from N87.38 trillion when Tinubu assumed office to N166.79 trillion by June 30, 2026. He also cited reports on killings and mass abductions to argue that the government had failed to protect lives and property. He called on Nigerians to reject Tinubu’s re-election bid, presenting the 2027 contest as a choice between continued hardship and a change of direction. “Tinubu priced you out of your own country. Atiku will bring you back in,” Ibrahim-Imam said. Mark, meanwhile, charged the campaign council to take its message to every state, local government, ward and community, warning members against taking voters for granted. “Our task is therefore bigger than winning an election. Our task is to present Nigerians with a credible alternative and give them the reason to believe and trust that the essence of governance is to protect them and make their lives better,” he said. He urged the party to run an issue-based campaign, engage Nigerians across ethnic and religious lines and avoid violence, while calling on the Independent National Electoral Commission and other electoral institutions to remain impartial and transparent. With the campaign council now inaugurated, the ADC faces the task of converting public frustration over economic hardship and insecurity into votes for the Atiku–Amaechi ticket in 2027. items.title: Anne Carson’s Point of View
items.description: This is an edition of the Books Briefing, our editors’ weekly guide to the best in books. Sign up for it here. The literature of ancient Greece and Rome seems to be in vogue. This summer, Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey turned Homer’s epic poems into best sellers, and yesterday the Nobel Prize was awarded to Anne Carson, a poet who has made a career of repurposing ancient-Greek works. Perhaps this resurgence has something to do with modern anxieties about the future; people tend to look back to the past in uncertain times. Although I’m glad to see the classics prominently displayed in bookstores, I’m not convinced that they hold a special kind of wisdom that contemporary writing can’t access. For evidence, I look to the work of Carson herself. The poet’s writing updates and remixes ancient verse and mythology, but she does not believe that the past is a manual for the present. As my colleague Walt Hunter explained this week in The Atlantic , “Rather than lulling us with history’s familiarity, she seduces us with its strangeness.” First, here are five new stories from The Atlantic ’s Books section: The year Anne Carson changed my life “Puffins,” a poem by Ange Mlinko “Something Like People,” a poem by Alexandra Petri “The Guardians,” a short story by Sebastian Junger Zombie originalism Take If Not, Winter , which is both a straightforward translation of the surviving poetry of Sappho and a playful, inventive collection of verse. Carson’s lines evoke the electric current of a marriage bed, the pleasure of beholding a girl’s delicate features, the pulse-quickening touch of the god Eros. These emotions are not lost to time—a reader might know, for example, what it means for a beloved’s voice to put “the heart in my chest on wings”—but there’s still a chasm between Sappho’s experiences and my own. I struggle to imagine the ancient poet’s relationships or daily concerns; similarly, if she could miraculously show up in my time, Sappho likely wouldn’t understand my job, my hobbies, or my marriage. (I imagine she’d be confused about why I describe myself with a name for people from her island: lesbian .) Carson’s 2010 book, Nox , accordion-printed on a single sheet of paper, mourns her brother’s death in part by employing the work of the Roman poet Catullus, who also suffered the death of a brother. Carson doesn’t imply that she and Catullus feel the same things. Her goal, instead, is to place herself in a tradition that “connects her to Catullus and a community of mourners as old as human history, one that we all belong to or will eventually join,” as I wrote last year . Communicating with the past has its limits. Carson has said that the classics offer some “glimpses of similarity” in a sea of “unbelievable otherness.” We’re separated by geography, culture, and time ; our values and societies are entirely different. But when the ancients wrote, they unspooled a thread that we can follow through the maze of time. It leads us through the “the gulf between the present and the past,” as Hunter writes, and brings us somewhere new and worthwhile. Graeme Mitchell / Redux Anne Carson’s Seductive Strangeness By Walt Hunter The winner of this year’s Nobel Prize in Literature makes ancient texts feel tantalizingly new. Read the full article. What to Read The Beauty of the Husband: A Fictional Essay in 29 Tangos , by Anne Carson The Beauty of the Husband is a poetic meditation on love, attraction, betrayal, and bitterness. Carson’s narrator has separated from her husband. Both are writers, though the narrator’s spouse, a womanizer and a liar, borrows heavily from her work—he even uses a phrase she has translated from Homer to open a letter he writes to his mistress. He is also, unfortunately, beautiful, and his “beauty convinces,” the narrator tells us. She confesses that she might be seduced by him all over again if he came near enough. But she keeps her distance, even as he routinely sends letters exalting their love. That space allows her to reflect honestly on their years together: “Why did nature give me over to this creature—don’t call it my choice, / I was ventured : / by some pure gravity of existence itself, / conspiracy of being!” she cries. In hindsight, the partnership feels inevitable; she had little control over loving him, but writing this book is a way to regain her autonomy, or so it appears. The Beauty of the Husband offers a vision of an uneven union, where one person’s outsize presence occupies, even consumes, the mind of the other. — Isle McElroy From our list: Seven books that explore how marriage really works Out Next Week 📚 Back: Essays on the Soul and Spine of America , by Lauren Michele Jackson 📚 The Last Best Place on the Internet: A Human History of Wikipedia , by Richard Cooke 📚 Reds: A Global History of Communism , by Paul Mason Your Weekend Read Illustration by Saskia Janssen The One Question I Can’t Stand at Restaurants By Brett Martin A man walks into a restaurant. He doesn’t have a reservation, but that shouldn’t be a problem; there are ample seats at the bar, visible just over the hostess’s shoulder. “Of course,” she says, smiling. “We can seat you right away.” As she gathers menus, he absorbs the pleasant hum of a busy dining room, breathes in the tantalizing smells from the semi-open kitchen. Then, the hostess stops, Columbo-like, to interrupt with one more question: “And what’s your phone number?” Read the full article. items.title: 2027: 30 days can’t erase over three years of hardship, Atiku tells Tinubu
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has dismissed President Bola Tinubu’s 30-day petrol discount as an inadequate response to years of economic hardship, saying Nigerians would hold the administration accountable in the 2027 general election. Atiku argued that a temporary reduction in petrol prices could not reverse the rising cost of food, transportation, electricity and business operations, insisting that Nigerians needed lasting relief rather than what he described as an election-season palliative. Speaking at the inauguration of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja on Friday, the former Vice President accused Tinubu of adopting the principle behind his proposed production subsidy after previously dismissing it, but failing to implement the policy’s essential safeguards. “Thirty days cannot erase three and a half years of hardship. Nigerians have heard your excuses and endured your failed promises. They are ready to judge your record,” Atiku said. He challenged the President to explain what would happen after the discount expired and whether transport fares and the cost of moving agricultural produce and running businesses would actually fall. “When I proposed targeted support to ease fuel costs, you called me ignorant of economic policy. Your government said it could not be done. Now, in a desperate and clumsy retreat, you have shamelessly embraced the principle you mocked. You owe me an apology,” he said. Atiku said his proposal would support petroleum products refined in Nigeria and sold locally, with government assistance capped, budgeted and independently audited, while excluding imported products. “My alternative is clear. Support petroleum products actually refined in Nigeria and sold to Nigerians. Cap the support. Put it in the budget. Audit it independently. Exclude imports. Show the public what it costs and what they save,” he said. He also called for measures to make food affordable, restore reliable electricity, create jobs, expand business opportunities and secure roads and farms, arguing that economic recovery must translate into tangible improvements in household welfare. Turning to the campaign council, Atiku charged members to take the ADC’s message to markets, motor parks, farms, campuses and communities, explain the party’s proposed policies and demonstrate how they would be funded. He described the 2027 election as a contest over the welfare of Nigerian families and urged eligible voters to mobilise behind the opposition party. “Another four years of Bola Tinubu means another four years of hunger, hardship and national decline,” he said. Atiku also demanded electoral reforms to protect votes, including immediate public access to polling-unit results, live broadcasts of state and national collation centres, and independent audits of election technology before and after elections. He called for an independent commission to investigate and prosecute electoral offences, as well as stronger penalties for vote suppression, result tampering and fraud. The ADC candidate further accused APC-controlled governments of restricting opposition campaigns, citing an attempt to prevent an opposition candidate from campaigning in Benue State. “There will be no ‘no-go’ areas in Nigeria. Opposition members are citizens with the constitutional right to move freely, express their views and campaign anywhere in the country,” he said. He vowed that the ADC would campaign across the country and resist attempts to prevent its candidates from reaching voters, saying the party would defend its rights through lawful means. In a challenge to Tinubu, Atiku urged the President to resign, arguing that the 30-day petrol discount could not erase the administration’s record on the economy. “After this latest admission of failure, the honourable thing to do is step down. Nigerians deserve a government that will do the work and make life affordable again,” he said. The post 2027: 30 days can’t erase over three years of hardship, Atiku tells Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GH¢800,000 goods destroyed as fire engulfs Kia Rhino truck on Apedwa-Kibi Road
items.description: A Kia Rhino truck loaded with refrigerators, generators, gas burners and chairs has been gutted by fire at Amanfrom on the Apedwa-Kibi road in the early hours of Thursday, October 8, with the estimated loss put at GH¢800,000. According to a Facebook post by the Ghana National Fire Service, the Kibi Fire Station received the distress call at 0314 hours and dispatched a crew led by ADO II Michael Kwakye. The crew arrived at 0332 hours to find the truck, registered GE 4273-26, fully engulfed in flames. Firefighters deployed two hose lines with foam, bringing the blaze under control at 0400 hours before extinguishing it completely at 0428 hours. The driver reportedly said he and two other occupants were travelling from Tema towards Kumasi when they stopped to rest and fell asleep. They were awakened by passers-by who alerted them to the fire and managed to escape through the windscreen. Fortunately, no casualties were recorded. The cause of the fire remains under investigation, while the estimated financial loss stands at GH¢800,000.

items.title: Chief Justice calls for supportive workplaces to address mental health stigma
items.description: Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie has urged employers to promote inclusive and supportive working environments to help combat stigma associated with mental health conditions. He made the call in a speech read on his behalf by Supreme Court Judge Sophia Rosetta Bernasko-Essah at this year’s World Mental Health Day celebration at the Court Complex in Accra on Friday, October 9. The event was jointly organised by the Greater Accra Regional Health Service and the Judicial Service of Ghana under the theme, “Lived Experiences Heard: Real Voices, Real Change.” In his address, the Chief Justice called for compassionate and accessible healthcare services, alongside institutional policies that prioritise mental well-being. He observed that stigma and the fear of judgement or exclusion often prevent people from speaking openly about their mental health challenges, urging the public to listen to their experiences with empathy and without prejudice. “We must listen with empathy; most importantly, we must let those experiences inform how we design policies, provide support, and respond to people going through difficult periods in their lives,” he said. He stressed the need for institutions to prioritise mental well-being and foster a workplace culture where employees feel comfortable seeking support without fear of being judged. “It is therefore important we recognise that mental well-being is not a peripheral matter; it is an essential part of a healthy, effective and human workplace. We must therefore create an institutional culture in which seeking help is not regarded as a weakness,” he said. Justice Baffoe-Bonnie said the mental well-being of judicial officers and staff was fundamental to an effective justice system, enabling them to perform their duties with clarity, integrity and compassion. The Chief Justice further highlighted the importance of mental health screening and assessments in preventing potential problems, identifying concerns at an early stage and ensuring timely intervention. “As a society we must move from merely sympathising with people experiencing mental health challenges to creating systems of support,” he said. He encouraged employers to sustain conversations about mental health in the workplace, promote mutual support among colleagues and create an environment in which staff feel comfortable seeking professional assistance when necessary. The World Mental Health Day celebration also featured screening for chronic medical conditions and mental health assessments for participants.

items.title: Sanctions : au nom de la défense de la «souveraineté américaine», Washington menace de porter l’estocade à la CPI
items.description: Dans un communique publie ce 9 octobre, le departement d'etat a annonce des « sanctions supplementaires » contre la Cour penale internationale (CPI), sous couvert de « defendre la souverainete americaine et ses citoyens contre la menace » que representerait cette institution. « L'Amerique n'a jamais adhere a cette cour. Nous n'avons pas besoin de cette cour et nous n'en voulons pas », a declare Marco Rubio dans une video publiee sur X, renvoyant au consensus en vigueur aux etats-Unis selon lequel la CPI ne saurait poursuivre des citoyens ou des soldats americains. Today, the Trump Administration is sanctioning the ICC. This action should encourage our Allies within the Court to work for solutions to end this threat to U.S. sovereignty forever. https://t.co/D86dCqLUaZ — Secretary Marco Rubio (@SecRubio) October 9, 2026 Le chef de la diplomatie americaine a explique que ces sanctions entreraient en application dans 180 jours, a moins qu'un accord ne soit conclu d'ici la. Elles entraîneraient l'interdiction de toute transaction financiere avec la CPI afin de « la couper de ses ressources et reduire sa capacite a operer » « Mettre fin a cette menace une fois pour toutes » « Notre message est clair : les etats-Unis et leur peuple ne relevent pas de la competence de ce simulacre de CPI. Les deux parties s'accordent sur ce point, mais seul le president Trump a la determination necessaire pour prendre les mesures qui s'imposent pour mettre fin a cette menace une fois pour toutes », a ajoute Marco Rubio. « Soit la CPI mettra fin a ses menaces, soit nous mettrons fin a la CPI. Nous attendons de nos allies, dont beaucoup font partie de la CPI et comptent sur les militaires americains pour leur defense, qu'ils maîtrisent cette cour vereuse », a-t-il poursuivi. Cette annonce survient, comme plusieurs medias occidentaux ont juge necessaire de le souligner, « quelques heures apres l'attribution du prix Nobel de la paix a l'ancienne juge sud-africaine Navi Pillay, recompensee notamment pour son travail au sein de cette juridiction » basee a La Haye. La CPI, qui n'est pas reconnue par une soixantaine de pays, dont les etats-Unis, la Russie et la Chine — tous trois membres permanents du Conseil de securite des Nations unies —, a denonce, par voie de communique, une « attaque contre l'etat de droit et les fondements memes de l'ordre juridique international » qui, selon elle, « porte un coup au principe fondamental selon lequel nul n'est au-dessus des lois ». Des sanctions « profondement regrettables », regrette une UE aux ordres L'Union europeenne, qui, visiblement, n'a nullement l'intention de defendre la CPI face a son « allie » etats-unien, bien que celle-ci siege dans l'un de ses etats membres, s'est contentee — egalement dans un communique — de se declarer « prete a prendre toutes les mesures necessaires pour permettre a la Cour de poursuivre son travail », estimant ces sanctions washingtoniennes « profondement regrettables ». Bien qu'ils applaudissent et vantent « l'independance » de la CPI lorsqu'elle cible leurs adversaires geopolitiques, les etats-Unis ont deja pris, a plusieurs reprises, des sanctions a l'encontre de la Cour et de ses magistrats. Plusieurs hauts responsables de cette juridiction s'etaient ainsi retrouves sous sanctions americaines apres l'emission, en novembre 2024, de mandats d'arret a l'encontre du Premier ministre israelien Benjamin Netanyahou et de son ancien ministre de la Defense, Yoav Gallant, dans le cadre de la guerre menee par Israel a Gaza. Un coup de pression similaire a celui exerce par Washington en 2020, deja sous Donald Trump, apres qu'une procureure s'etait penchee sur les exactions commises par l'armee americaine lors de l'invasion de l'Afghanistan. Par ailleurs, depuis 2002, une loi federale donne au president americain carte blanche pour « utiliser tous les moyens necessaires et appropries pour obtenir la liberation » d'un citoyen — ou d'un « allie » — des etats-Unis qui viendrait a etre detenu par la CPI, y compris par la force militaire. Un texte, promulgue sous George W. Bush, qui fut surnomme « The Hague Invasion Act ».

items.title: NVI CEO defends GH¢13m spending on training, workshops and conferences
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the National Vaccine Institute, Dr. Sodzi Sodzi-Tettey, has defended the Institute’s GH¢13 million expenditure on training, workshops and conferences in 2025, insisting the activities are critical to its mandate and capital-intensive. This follows concerns raised by the Public Accounts Committee after the Auditor-General reported a financial downturn, with the Institute moving from a profit of 36 million Ghana cedis to a loss of 21 million cedis within the financial year. Appearing before the Committee, Dr Sodzi-Tettey defended the expenditure, explaining that much of the Institute’s work involves building the capacity of researchers, manufacturers and regulators to support the development of Ghana’s vaccine industry. He said the Institute’s mandate required significant investment in training and knowledge-sharing activities because the country’s vaccine ecosystem lacked the technical capacity needed to support local vaccine manufacturing. Dr Sodzi-Tettey explained that the Institute’s activities extended beyond conventional training programmes to include efforts to develop expertise across the various stages of vaccine research, production and regulation. He said the Institute worked with researchers at universities across the country, manufacturers whose production capabilities needed improvement, and regulators who required specialised knowledge to perform their duties effectively. He added that manufacturers and regulatory institutions also needed support to develop the technical expertise required to establish a sustainable domestic vaccine industry. According to him, activities involving these groups could be classified under training, seminars and conferences in the Institute’s financial records, contributing to the substantial amount recorded under those expenditure headings. Institute cites limited technical capacity Dr Sodzi-Tettey argued that developing vaccine manufacturing capacity was a complex and expensive undertaking that could not be achieved within a short period. He described vaccine manufacturing as one of the weakest areas of Ghana’s vaccine ecosystem, saying the country lacked the technical expertise and infrastructure required to undertake several specialised processes independently. “Vaccine manufacturing is not something that you would get up and then suddenly realise that you have the capacity to do it. It is our weakest area in the vaccine ecosystem,” he said. To illustrate the skills gap, he cited the production of snake venom antiserum, explaining that the Institute had to bring in experts from India to conduct some of the required tests. He said foreign specialists were also needed to support certain animal studies undertaken as part of the process of developing manufacturing capabilities. “In the course of manufacturing the snake venom antiserum, we have to bring in experts from India to be able to do some of the tests that are required,” he told the Committee. “In some of the animal studies that we have to do to be able to manufacture the vaccines, experts have to be brought in from outside of the country to support us,” he added. The CEO said Ghana had several young scientists whose skills could be developed to meet the country’s future vaccine research and manufacturing needs. However, he maintained that formal education alone was insufficient to provide all the specialised expertise required for vaccine production, making continuous training and capacity development necessary. “We have some young scientists for sure, but their capacities will have to be built now and going into the future, to be able to do what we want them to do,” he said. He stressed that the sector required substantial investment because the technical skills and facilities needed to manufacture vaccines were not readily available locally. “The thing about these areas is that they are all capital-intensive. They are really capital-intensive, and the capacity is not there. So you do have to train people to be able to do it, and that’s where a lot of the budget is going into,” Dr Sodzi-Tettey said. Community engagement forms part of the mandate Beyond scientific research and manufacturing, the CEO said the Institute also engaged communities to assess public understanding of, and willingness to accept, vaccines manufactured locally. He explained that such engagements were necessary to understand public attitudes towards locally produced vaccines and support efforts to build confidence in domestic vaccine development. The activities, he suggested, formed part of the broader work required to establish a functional vaccine ecosystem in Ghana, alongside building the capabilities of researchers, manufacturers and regulators.

items.title: Ghana targets first locally manufactured vaccine by 2027
items.description: Ghana is expected to produce its first locally manufactured vaccine by 2027, with production processes currently underway at Atlantic Lifesciences Limited. Chief Executive Officer of the National Vaccine Institute (NVI), Dr Sodzi Sodzi-Tettey, disclosed this to journalists in Parliament, saying the project was progressing through a partnership involving local scientific institutions, private manufacturers and an Indonesian pharmaceutical company. He said the initiative was expected to strengthen Ghana’s domestic vaccine manufacturing capacity and reduce its reliance on imported vaccines. “Ghana is on track to manufacture the first vaccine in 2027, and that is tetanus-diphtheria vaccine,” Dr Sodzi-Tettey said. He explained that the National Vaccine Institute had assembled a team of experts from Ghana, including officials from the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) and private manufacturers, who travelled to Indonesia to facilitate the technology transfer required for local production. According to him, the team signed a technology transfer agreement and established links between the regulatory authorities of Ghana and Indonesia to support the manufacturing process. Dr Sodzi-Tettey said the agreement was a critical step towards achieving the country’s vaccine production ambitions, although the associated expenditure might appear in financial records as costs for workshops or meetings. “If you want to analyse where that falls in a financial statement, it will appear to you as a workshop or as a meeting, but that meeting had been very critical because then it freed up about US$400,000 from the Indonesian government to support the vaccine manufacturing in the country,” he said. He added that most of the relevant materials had arrived in Ghana, with manufacturing processes now underway at Atlantic Lifesciences Limited. Partnership drives vaccine production The CEO said the project was being implemented through a partnership involving the National Vaccine Institute, Atlantic Lifesciences Limited, the Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research and PT Bio Farma of Indonesia. The collaboration is expected to combine local scientific expertise and manufacturing capacity with technical support from Indonesia to advance Ghana’s efforts to produce vaccines domestically. Dr Sodzi-Tettey expressed optimism that the partnership would deliver the country’s first locally manufactured tetanus-diphtheria vaccine next year. “The bulk has arrived in the country; the manufacturing processes are underway at Atlantic Lifesciences. It is a partnership between National Vaccine Institute, Atlantic Lifesciences, Noguchi Memorial Institute and PT Bio Farma of Indonesia, and God willing, next year we should be able to come up with a vaccine,” he said. The initiative forms part of broader efforts to establish a sustainable vaccine manufacturing ecosystem in Ghana, including developing technical expertise, strengthening regulatory capacity and building local production capabilities. Beyond the tetanus-diphtheria vaccine project, Dr Sodzi-Tettey said the National Vaccine Institute had other plans for seed funding pledged by President John Dramani Mahama. The planned investments are expected to complement ongoing work with local and international partners as the country seeks to strengthen its position in vaccine research and production. If the current timeline is achieved, the production of a locally manufactured tetanus-diphtheria vaccine by 2027 would mark a significant milestone in Ghana’s efforts to develop domestic vaccine manufacturing capacity.

items.title: For Good Connections Day : Orange Burkina sensibilise les jeunes à un usage responsable du numérique
items.description: Dans le cadre de sa démarche en faveur d’un usage responsable du numérique, Orange Burkina Faso a lancé, ce 8 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la deuxième édition du « For Good Connections Day » . L’initiative entend sensibiliser les jeunes aux risques et aux dérives liés à l’utilisation du numérique, tout en les outillant pour en faire un usage plus responsable et bénéfique à leur bien-être. Organisé simultanément dans plusieurs pays du groupe Orange autour d’une même cause, le « For Good Connections Day » met l’accent sur la sensibilisation des jeunes aux enjeux liés aux usages numériques. Au Burkina Faso, l’activité, à la fois ludique, éducative et sportive, a réuni environ 200 jeunes. Le programme cible principalement les adolescents âgés de 11 à 18 ans. Au cours de la rencontre, une ingénieure en informatique a échangé avec les participants sur les enjeux liés au numérique et les bonnes pratiques à adopter. Visiblement intéressés, les jeunes ont pris une part active à la séance à travers des questions et des contributions. Prévenir les risques et responsabiliser les jeunes Ousmane Soumbougma, chef de département Orange Digital Center Burkina, a expliqué que l’enjeu est d’anticiper les risques liés aux usages numériques et de responsabiliser les jeunes. « On a besoin que cette utilisation soit responsable et sécurisée. Donc l’idée, c’est de protéger leur avenir et de les amener à être responsables quand ils sont sur les réseaux sociaux », a-t-il expliqué. La campagne, à l’en croire, a déjà permis de toucher environ 4 200 jeunes depuis le début de l’année, notamment à Ouahigouya, Bobo-Dioulasso, Banfora et Fada. Les participants sont également encouragés à devenir des relais auprès de leurs pairs et de leurs proches. À Ouagadougou, les activités combinent sport, animation et mises en situation. Les jeunes sont placés face à différents scénarios et amenés à faire des choix, avant d’en mesurer les conséquences. Une approche participative destinée à favoriser l’assimilation des messages de sensibilisation. Une responsabilité partagée autour des usages numériques Le directeur de la réglementation des communications électroniques au ministère en charge de la Transition digitale, Dr Ibrahim Patrick Congo, a salué l’initiative portée par Orange Burkina Faso. Il a insisté sur la nécessité d’une implication collective pour mieux accompagner les jeunes dans l’univers numérique. « L’univers numérique est un univers où tout le monde doit jouer son rôle. Le ministère représentant l’État qui élabore les règles et protège, les opérateurs comme Orange qui assument ses responsabilités, et les enseignants et les parents qui doivent accompagner pour donner tous les outils nécessaires à nos enfants afin qu’ils profitent de cet univers, de cet environnement plein de potentialité, mais également plein de danger » , a-t-il ajouté. Le représentant du ministère a par ailleurs relevé plusieurs menaces auxquelles les jeunes peuvent être exposés en ligne, notamment le cyberharcèlement, l’escroquerie et l’usurpation de données. Pour lui, l’éducation aux risques numériques doit permettre aux jeunes de mieux faire face à ces menaces et de tirer parti des opportunités offertes par Internet. Élève en classe de seconde C au lycée Marien-Gouabi, Djao Draman a également pris part à la séance de sensibilisation. Il dit avoir particulièrement retenu les notions relatives à la protection des données à caractère personnel et à la maîtrise du temps passé sur les réseaux sociaux. « Pour protéger ses données à caractère personnel, il faut tout d’abord utiliser consciencieusement les réseaux sociaux, éviter de partager des contenus qui portent atteinte à l’intégrité de quiconque sur ces mêmes réseaux sociaux » , a-t-il confié. Pour le jeune élève, l’utilisation du numérique doit aussi rester compatible avec les exigences scolaires. Il recommande ainsi de limiter le temps d’écran et de privilégier les études, tout en recourant à Internet lorsque cela est nécessaire pour les recherches scolaires. Éléonore Savadogo Faso7 L’article For Good Connections Day : Orange Burkina sensibilise les jeunes à un usage responsable du numérique est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Outrage over plan to livestream US military firing squad execution
items.description: Condemnation of the Pentagon’s plan to livestream the firing squad execution of a convicted military base mass shooter escalated Friday, with the UN saying it would amount to torture and US lawmakers from both parties slamming the move. Nidal Hasan’s execution — which is scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 — is set to be the first by US military firing squad since 1945. Representative Austin Scott, a member of US President Donald Trump’s Republican Party, said he supported executing Hasan but that “livestreaming executions is what jihadists do. America is better than that.” Senator Jack Reed, the top Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, said broadcasting the execution would be “a barbaric spectacle” that would give Hasan “more attention and more control” and “a global platform to amplify his hateful, anti-American message.” “This is a gift to anti-American terrorist recruiters,” Reed said. Trump on Friday backed the execution — saying Hasan “deserves it” and branding him a “maniac” — but did not comment on the plan to publicize it. A Pentagon official told AFP the previous day that the execution would be streamed live, after US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said “we’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public.” Later, Hegseth wrote “Correct” when retweeting a media report about the planned livestream. The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights condemned the move, saying in a message sent to AFP on Friday that “the livestreaming of an execution is tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture.” Archbishop Paul Coakley, president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops, said it was a “barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered.” – ‘Compound the cruelty’ – Hegseth said it would be the military’s first firing squad execution since World War II — a reference to the case of Eddie Slovik, who was put to death for desertion in 1945. “People need to understand that… there’s serious consequence for these types of things,” Hegseth said in a video disseminated Thursday on official Pentagon X accounts. “I kind of like the mentality we had in World War II, which was win, which was understand when the enemy attacks you, you need to stand your ground,” Hegseth said. The last US military execution was carried out in 1961, when John Bennett was hanged for rape and attempted murder. The Death Penalty Information Center says that 135 soldiers have been executed by the US military since 1916. According to rights group Amnesty International, at least 17 public executions are known to have been carried out in 2025 — six in Afghanistan and 11 in Iran. Amnesty’s Justin Mazzola said Friday that the death penalty is “a violation of human rights,” and that streaming Hasan’s execution “would only compound the cruelty.” Twelve of the 13 people Hasan killed and 30 of those he wounded were soldiers.He was shot and partially paralyzed by a civilian police officer who responded to the attack. Hasan chose to conduct his own defense during the trial but called no witnesses and gave no testimony, and made no attempt to deny the charges. He was sentenced to death by a military jury in 2013. Court-appointed defense attorneys expressed concern that he was seeking execution. The court that convicted Hasan was told he was opposed to the US military’s occupations of Iraq and Afghanistan, and that he had spoken online with an alleged Al-Qaeda figure, radical cleric Anwar al-Awlaki, an American citizen subsequently killed in a US drone strike in Yemen. While mass shootings in the United States are common, they are relatively rare at military facilities. The furor over Hasan’s impending execution comes just days after convicted murderer Christa Pike survived a botched execution in the US state of Tennessee, fueling debate about the death penalty in the country. items.title: Forum de Beijing : la gouvernance urbaine à l’ère du numérique en débat
items.description: Les technologies façonnent à un rythme accéléré le fonctionnement des sociétés. Chaque jour, elles conquièrent petit à petit tous les compartiments de la vie sociale. Autant elles apportent des facilités extraordinaires dans le quotidien des populations, autant elles suscitent des inquiétudes quant à leur omniprésence dans toutes les sphères sociales. Leur appropriation conséquente et leur régulation sont au cœur des préoccupations tant au niveau étatique qu'à l'échelle de la gouvernance locale. Le numérique est devenu une partie intégrante dans le processus de modernisation des villes partout dans le monde. Il est inconcevable d'implémenter de nos jours une gouvernance urbaine sans une prise en compte des technologies. Les villes, centres névralgiques de toutes les révolutions et évolutions sociales, sont les baromètres à travers lesquels l'on perçoit véritablement l'influence du numérique sur le quotidien des populations. Dans la dynamique de promouvoir une réflexion féconde sur la gouvernance urbaine, la quatrième édition du Forum de Beijing sur la réponse rapide aux plaintes du public se tiendra les 12 et 13 octobre 2026 sur le thème « L'ère du numérique et de l'intelligence artificielle et la ville au service des citoyens ». L'urbanisation est au cœur du développement de la modernisation et les enjeux futurs de la planète s'observent à partir des villes. Des données officielles stipulent que d'ici à 2050, 70% de la population mondiale sera urbaine. C'est dire combien les villes concentrent à elles seules les questions inhérentes à la démographie, à la mobilité, à la sécurité, à la gestion des ressources, bref à la gouvernance. Anticiper les réponses sur ces enjeux est l'un des objectifs visés par le Forum de Beijing. De ce fait, la place du numérique dans la gouvernance urbaine est primordiale. Depuis quelques années, la gestion de grandes villes, à travers le monde, a connu une nette amélioration grâce à l'intervention des technologies. Une ville comme Beijing a mis en place un système de gestion des plaintes des citoyens et des entreprises à travers la ligne d'assistance téléphonique 12345. Grâce à ce dispositif, les services habilités à apporter des réponses aux requêtes des citoyens arrivent à remplir leurs missions avec plus d'efficacité. Grâce à l'appui du numérique, Beijing, ville aux 21 millions d'habitants, parvient à optimiser son travail en exploitant et en analysant efficacement les données qui se rapportent aux conditions de vie de la population. Ainsi, des solutions appropriées sont apportées aux difficultés des citadins. L'outil numérique, conjugué à une qualité de la gouvernance, ouvre des perspectives intéressantes pour des villes futures en phase avec les besoins des habitants. Par exemple, la Zone de développement économique et technologique de Beijing, connue sous le nom de « Beijing E-Town », est devenue un pôle d'intelligence numérique où informatique en nuage, mégadonnées et intelligence artificielle sont mises à contribution pour offrir toute une gamme variée de services aux citoyens. À ce titre, il importe d'encourager les regards croisés autour de cette technologie incontournable. La sécurité est également une dimension essentielle qui indique qu'une ville rassure et donne envie d'y résider ou de la visiter. En plus d'aider à résoudre les difficultés des citadins, les technologies participent à une meilleure sécurisation des villes. La gouvernance sécuritaire des villes s'est significativement améliorée en Chine grâce au numérique faisant du pays l'une des destinations les plus sûres au monde. Le Rapport sur l'indice de sécurité publique mondiale (2025-2026) a indiqué que la Chine occupe la première place du classement avec 84,62 points. À cela, il faut ajouter le sentiment de sécurité perçu à l'unanimité par ceux qui visitent la Chine. Des témoignages recueillis auprès de voyageurs étrangers, il ressort que la sécurité est perceptible partout dans les villes chinoises. La gouvernance urbaine doit être comprise comme un processus national qui s'inscrit en droite ligne des objectifs de l'initiative Chine pacifique. Pour les autorités chinoises, il s'agit de travailler ardemment « pour rendre le pays plus sûr, la société plus ordonnée, la gouvernance plus efficace et la population plus satisfaite, que la modernisation à la chinoise avance de manière stable et durable.» C'est pourquoi le Forum de Beijing se veut un cadre de rencontre et partage des meilleures pratiques en matière de gouvernance urbaine à l'aune du numérique et de l'intelligence artificielle. À ce rendez-vous où sont attendus plus de 3 200 invités dont plus de 240 participants internationaux venus de plus de 70 pays, il s'agira de nourrir la réflexion autour de thématiques comme « Raffinement et excellence : modèles de gouvernance de précision et durabilité urbaine », « Aspirations et bien commun : évolution de la bonne gouvernance et élévation de la civilisation urbaine », « Sagesse et partage : l'intelligence numérique au service de la modernisation de la gouvernance urbaine », « Échanges et intégration : gouvernance collaborative et ouverture et inclusivité des villes »… À la lecture de ces thématiques variées, l'on voit combien la gouvernance urbaine est complexe d'autant plus qu'elle concentre de nombreux défis. Le numérique apparaît donc une nouvelle dynamique qui offre une palette d'approches pour gouverner judicieusement les villes avec à la clé des services de qualité offerts aux citoyens. L'outil technologique pourrait également favoriser une meilleure prise en compte des questions écologiques, de mobilité urbaine, de sécurité, d'inclusion sociale, d'architecture et de préservation du patrimoine culturel dans la gouvernance urbaine. Des cadres d'échanges comme le Forum de Beijing ouvrent des pistes réflexives pour mieux appréhender l'avenir des sociétés qui doit désormais se conjuguer avec le numérique. Karim BADOLO CGTN Français

items.title: 2027: Sanction Amaechi now; Wike urges INEC
items.description: … Links FCT NLC chairman to ADC, says teachers’ strike is political blackmail By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja The minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has demanded action from the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC against the African Democratic Congress ADC vice presidential candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, over his remarks about President Bola Tinubu and his supporters. Wike spoke on Friday in Abuja, shortly after a closed-door meeting with the chairmen of the six Area Councils and security operatives. He said he had not heard that INEC had drawn Amaechi’s attention to his utterances. “Many Nigerians have called INEC to sanction political parties and candidates or some politicians who, in their campaigns, incite the public or raise matters that are not issue-based. We have been told to go on campaigns based on issues. What are you going to do about the people attacking personality or insulting individuals? Up till now, I have not heard that INEC has been able to call or draw the attention of the vice presidential candidate of the ADC, Rotimi Amaechi, to this,” the minister said. He also challenged the media to press the opposition for accountability instead of staying neutral in the face of what he called unsubstantiated insults against the president and his supporters. Wike raised questions about projects during Amaechi’s time as governor of Rivers State, including a multi-million-dollar hospital, the state monorail, the sale of a state-owned gas turbine and a state-wide fumigation contract. “I challenge him. Ask him the $10 million you paid to a Cuban company to fumigate Rivers State so there will be no mosquito bite. Up till now, mosquitoes have been biting Rivers people, including myself. Ask him, ‘The ₦68 billion monorail – where is the monorail?’ Ask him, Where is the $308 million with which you sold our gas turbine?” he said. He warned that continued attacks on the president and his supporters would meet resistance from supporters across the country, particularly in Rivers State, and added that thieves and lunatics will not preside over Nigeria. “If he continues along this line, it may be difficult for him to campaign in Rivers. And I want somebody to go and write it down. Because we will not take that. We will not,” he said. On the strike declared by the FCT Chapter of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Wike described it as a politically motivated attempt to blackmail the administration. He said the FCT Administration had met all its obligations to local government workers and teachers. “We want to state categorically and let it be known to the public that this so-called strike declaration is political, and we will not accept it. We will not accept it because there’s no basis for anybody to call for a strike. We don’t have any issue with anybody, either be it the area council, local education, primary authority, or secondary schools; we have no issues,” he said. He announced the immediate implementation of a “no work, no pay” policy across all Area Councils. The minister said major education bodies, including the Universal Basic Education Board (UBEB), had explicitly dissociated themselves from the strike because existing agreements were already being carried out. He said the FCT NLC Chairman, Hon. Stephen Knabayi, was a candidate of the ADC in the last Area Council elections and warned against using industrial action for political gain. “And you can see his interest trying to see that FCT is in crisis, and then he wants to use it as a political tool that FCT teachers are at home, and nobody is teaching students; how can you now come and vote for a government when the pupils are at home? We cannot accept that blackmail. We won’t accept it. “I have told everybody, and I have told Labour, ‘Look, if you want to involve yourself in politics, you are free to, but then excuse yourself from the leadership of the union so you don’t politicise it,'” he said. Wike also ordered a crackdown on unapproved beer parlours along the Guzape-Asokoro axis, directing that they be dismantled before they become security liabilities. The post 2027: Sanction Amaechi now; Wike urges INEC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: « Octobre rose » à la Police nationale : dépistage des cancers et inauguration d’une maternité à Dakar
items.description: La Police nationale a célébré « Octobre rose », mardi 6 octobre, au Camp Abdou Diassé de Dakar, par une journée de dépistage et de consultations gratuites. La cérémonie, présidée par le directeur général de la Police nationale, Mame Seydou Ndour, en présence de la mission médicale chinoise, a été marquée par l’inauguration de la maternité du service de santé de la police. La célébration d’ « Octobre rose » à la Police nationale a pris une dimension particulière au Camp Abdou Diassé de Dakar. En plus des activités de dépistage des cancers du sein et du col de l’utérus, de consultations gratuites, de vaccination des enfants de 9 à 14 ans et d’un don de sang, la Police nationale a inauguré la maternité de son Service de santé. Une double initiative placée sous le signe de la prévention et du bien-être des personnels, notamment des femmes. Avec comme marraine la commissaire de police à la retraite Aby Diallo, la cérémonie a été organisée en partenariat avec la mission médicale chinoise, en présence du directeur général de la Police, Mame Seydou Ndour, et de hauts responsables de l’institution. Dans ce cadre, le chef de la Division genre de la Police nationale, la commissaire de police Binetou Guissé, a rappelé la priorité accordée à la santé des femmes en uniforme. D’après cette dernière, les femmes policières, malgré leurs responsabilités professionnelles, doivent également veiller à leur propre santé. D’où la nécessité, pour elle, de faire du dépistage un réflexe. « Se faire dépister, ce n’est pas avoir peur de la maladie. C’est choisir de prendre sa santé en main », a-t-elle souligné. Profitant de l’occasion, Mme Guissé a rendu hommage à la marraine de la journée, l’ancienne commissaire divisionnaire Aby Diallo, présentée comme une pionnière ayant ouvert la voie aux générations de femmes policières. Très émue, Mmz Diallo a salué les progrès accomplis par l’institution depuis l’intégration des premières femmes dans ses rangs, il y a plus de quatre décennies. « Cela veut dire que la police a fait beaucoup de progrès et a pris en compte le genre », a-t-elle déclaré, avant de souhaiter « plein succès » à la maternité inaugurée à l’occasion en vue de répondre aux attentes du personnel féminin et de la population. Présidant la rencontre, l’inspecteur général de police Mame Seydou Ndour a souligné la portée de cette double cérémonie. Selon lui, cette journée « témoigne de la volonté constante de la hiérarchie policière de placer la santé, le bien-être et la dignité des personnels, particulièrement des femmes, au cœur de ses préoccupations ». Il s’est félicité des équipements de dernière génération dont la maternité est dotée au grand bénéfice, dit-il, du personnel de la police, mais aussi des populations de Dakar. Souleymane WANE

items.title: Crise énergétique à Kiev : Zelensky accuse le maire, qui contre-attaque sur la corruption dans son entourage
items.description: Le 9 octobre, Volodymyr Zelensky a mis en cause la mairie de Kiev, lui reprochant de ne pas avoir pris les mesures necessaires pour preparer la capitale aux frappes sur le reseau energetique. Apres une reunion avec des responsables civils et militaires, il a declare : « Des tâches specifiques ont ete definies pour la ville de Kiev en raison de la non-execution presque totale des mesures necessaires par les autorites municipales. » Ces accusations interviennent alors que les frappes russes ont de nouveau fortement endommage les installations energetiques ukrainiennes. Depuis le 7 octobre, des coupures d'eau et d'electricite touchent Kiev. Le lendemain, les trois lignes du metro ont ete immobilisees et le trafic des tramways et trolleybus perturbe. Zelensky a lui-meme reconnu l'etendue des degâts et denonce des retards dans les preparatifs de l'hiver. Les autorites ukrainiennes ont actualise leurs demandes d'equipements energetiques et antiaeriens aupres de leurs partenaires europeens. Le ministere russe de la Defense affirme que ses frappes viennent en reponse a l'intensification des attaques ukrainiennes contre les infrastructures civiles sur le territoire russe. Klitchko evoque un « mode de survie » Le 8 octobre, Vitali Klitchko, maire de Kiev, avait averti que la capitale entrait en « mode de survie ». Le maire redoute une crise majeure si les difficultes d'approvisionnement en eau se prolongent, particulierement a l'approche de l'hiver. La municipalite prepare des reserves d'eau potable, de nourriture et de carburant, ainsi que des solutions de chauffage de secours. Klitchko a recommande aux habitants pouvant etre heberges par des proches hors de Kiev de quitter la ville. Il a toutefois precise qu'aucune evacuation generale n'etait annoncee. Meme avec des reserves, souligne-t-il, la capitale pourrait se retrouver en difficulte si la defense antiaerienne ne parvenait pas a intercepter les frappes. Le maire rejette les accusations de mauvaise preparation et invoque le manque de temps, de financements et de personnel. Il conteste que la responsabilite de la crise soit imputee aux seuls services municipaux. « La recherche de boucs emissaires ne donnera pas davantage de chaleur aux habitants », a-t-il declare. L'entourage presidentiel accuse de corruption La confrontation depasse la seule gestion du reseau electrique. Dans un entretien, Klitchko a denonce la corruption qu'il attribue a l'entourage presidentiel. Selon lui, ces pratiques affaiblissent l'Ukraine et compromettent la confiance des allies etrangers, essentielle en temps de conflit. Il a decrit cette corruption presumee comme un « poison » pour son pays. Les desaccords entre les deux responsables ne datent pas d'hier. Lors de precedentes coupures de courant, Zelensky avait deja reproche au maire son manque de reactivite. Klitchko avait denonce des attaques politiques a son encontre et accuse le pouvoir central d'entretenir des conflits avec les autorites locales. Les nouveaux degâts energetiques ramenent cette rivalite au premier plan. Alors que les autorites ukrainiennes redoutent un hiver difficile, les accusations de negligence et de corruption alimentent une confrontation publique entre la presidence et la mairie de Kiev.
